A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 27-page versions of the same PQMass paper, including Appendices A–I. Full-text and rendered-page comparisons support reliable assessment.

before.justification: v3 reports original null tests, sampling-method evaluations, image-generation experiments, and additional empirical studies in the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains the same original experimental results in Section 3 and the appendices, including sampling comparisons and generative-model evaluations.

M1.justification: The Voronoi partitioning, reference-point selection, multinomial comparison, Pearson chi-squared statistic, and permutation-test procedure are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions retain identical coverage of synthetic distributions, image datasets, time series, Adult Census tabular data, astrophysical data, and protein sequences. No dataset or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout, including Wasserstein, MMD, JSD, FID, FLD, novelty metrics, and the weighted and unweighted nearest-neighbor tests in Appendix H.

E3.justification: Sample sizes, splits, metrics, model configurations, training budgets, and evaluation procedures are identical. For example, both retain the 100-epoch MNIST experiment comparing 2,000 generated and 2,000 test samples.

E4.justification: The reference-count and distance-metric ablations, mode-dropping and small-mode tests, noise sensitivity, memorization analysis, sample visualizations, and permutation-test analyses are all retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Repeated-run information and uncertainty reporting are identical, including the 20 reference-point repetitions and standard deviations in Section 3.2, repeated MNIST training experiments, and appendix significance reporting.

E6.justification: All numerical results, plotted findings, rankings, and qualitative observations are unchanged. Tables 1–6 and the result figures, including those in the appendices, are identical.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, equations, Propositions 2.1 and 2.2 and their proofs, and Appendix I permutation-test reasoning are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about likelihood-free distribution comparison, assessing generative models, computational efficiency, and operation without feature extraction.

C2.justification: Interpretations and qualifications are unchanged, including Section 4's limitations concerning sample size, tessellation choice, independent samples, and distance metrics, and Appendix I's discussion of reused samples.

D1.justification: Implementation information, Appendix D model hyperparameters, preprocessing, hardware and runtime disclosures, and code/data access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography, and positioning relative to earlier methods are identical. The author-name update does not change the paper's relationship to prior research.

P1.justification: Page 1 changes the displayed author name from Nikolay Malkin to Esmeralda S. Whitammer, and page 11 changes the acknowledgment initials from N.M. to E.S.W. The arXiv version/date stamp also changes; scientific prose and section organization remain identical.

P2.justification: All 23 figures and six tables retain their content, captions, axes, legends, structure, and placement. There is no restructuring of the page layout beyond the text substitutions recorded under P1.

improvement.justification: v4 updates author identification, acknowledgment initials, and the arXiv stamp while preserving the scientific content and all appendix evidence. These administrative edits leave the paper's scientific support, reproducibility information, and explanatory quality unchanged.
